result_text:
I added `analyzeLandscape` as a second name for the landscape command. It compiles, but I did not run it: launching the built CLI needs approval I wasn't given, and the `cli` module has no tests.

**Changes:**
- **`cli/.../Commands.java`**: new `ANALYZE_LANDSCAPE` name and description (the landscape counterpart of the analysis commands, same as `updateLandscape`). It is listed in the no-argument usage overview with the same landscape options.
- **`cli/.../CommandLineInterface.java`**: the dispatch accepts either name and runs the same `updateLandscape` code path, so options and behaviour are identical. For `-help`, the usage line shows the name the user typed, and `analyzeLandscape` gets its own description. `updateLandscape -help` prints its original description.
- **`README.md`**: the README had no command descriptions, so I added a short "Commands" section covering `analyzeLandscape` and `updateLandscape` (plus `init` and `generateReports`).

**Not verified:** I did not run `analyzeLandscape -help`, `updateLandscape -help`, or an end-to-end landscape run, so the help output and the `index.html` creation are checked by reading the code only. `CLAUDE.md` still lists only `updateLandscape` among the main commands; I left it alone. Nothing is committed.
